title: What a market economic system is

blocks.heading: What this section asks you to do
blocks.text: Define the market economic system and identify its features: who owns resources, who takes production decisions, and what role prices play in allocating those resources.

blocks.heading: The definition
blocks.text: A market economic system is an economic system in which resources are allocated through the price mechanism: most resources are privately owned, households and firms take the production decisions, and prices formed by demand and supply determine what is produced, how it is produced and for whom. No central authority draws up a plan of what the country should make. Instead, the answers to the three questions every economy faces - what, how and for whom to produce - emerge from the buying and selling of millions of households and firms. In Namibia, the fruit traded at the open market in Oshakati illustrates the idea: no official instructs anyone to bring mangoes, yet sellers bring them, buyers pay for them, and the price settles where the quantity sellers bring meets the quantity buyers want.

blocks.heading: The features to name in an answer
blocks.text: An answer that identifies the features of a market system names four things. Private ownership: most resources - land, shops, machines - belong to private people and firms, not to the state. Decentralised decisions: each household decides what to buy and each firm decides what to produce, so choices are made by the people living with them rather than by a planning office. The profit motive: firms produce because they expect to earn profit, which is the reward that keeps them responding to what buyers want. Freely moving prices: prices rise and fall with demand and supply, and it is these price movements that tell resources where to go. Germany and the Netherlands operate largely this way in their retail sectors: a shop owner in Hamburg decides stock, sets prices to clear it, and answers to no ministry for the choice.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The price mechanism this topic defines is the machinery of topic 2.5, where demand and supply set the equilibrium price; the mixed economic system of topic 2.11 is the halfway house most countries, Namibia among them, actually run; and topic 2.10 collects the cases where this machinery misfires.
